sheets.title: The vault on a phone — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: Two more rows of the frame go, and neither carried anything the screen did not already say. The statusline was a full-width bar under the tab bar for things looked at rarely; it is now one key in the bar the phone already has at the top. The breadcrumb read "Vault" under a tab bar marking Vault — a breadcrumb with one item is a label, and it is the one label the nav already carries.

sheets.title: The smallest phone — 320 × 568
sheets.caption: On a 568px screen those two rows were an eighth of everything. Chrome is the top bar and the tab bar, and nothing else.

sheets.title: Where the status bar went — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: Notifications, help, the keymap and the five connectors, behind the top bar's one overflow key — where an overflow belongs. It carries a dot whenever something inside wants attention, so nothing that was glanceable stopped being glanceable. Not a sixth tab: that was tried first and clipped "Connections" to "Connecti…" at every phone width, because the label clamp sizes type against the bar, which does not shrink when a column is added.
sheets.after: one key, named rows behind it

sheets.title: Rotated — 844 × 390
sheets.caption: Landscape has 390px of height and had a special case to make two bottom bars share a row. There is one bar now, so the special case went with the second one.
sheets.before: two bars sharing a row, plus a crumb

sheets.title: Desktop keeps its strip — 1280 × 800
sheets.caption: Captured with a mouse, not an emulated phone. The statusline is still seven keys and the five connector glyphs are still the strip: a glance costs nothing where there is room for it. The only change here is the one-item breadcrumb, which the rail already marked.
